activities.title: Ionic bonding: sodium gives an electron away

differentiation.support: Provide the student notes open at the lattice definition so learners can follow how each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions before they try to point at a molecule.

activities.title: Metallic bonding: a sea of electrons

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why molten sodium chloride conducts electricity but solid sodium chloride does not before they take the exit ticket.

assessmentPoints: Transfer answers in the opening activity
Lattice answers in the second activity and the closing worksheet
successCriteria: I can say sodium gives its outer electron to chlorine, forming a positive sodium ion and a negative chloride ion
I can describe an ionic compound as a giant lattice of ions, with the formula giving only the ratio
objectives.text: Describe ionic bonding as electron transfer forming a giant lattice of ions

assessmentPoints: Chlorine molecule answers in the third activity
Covalent answers in the closing exit ticket
successCriteria: I can explain that a covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons counted by both atoms
I can say sharing forms separate molecules and makes no ions
objectives.text: Describe covalent bonding as shared pairs of electrons forming molecules

assessmentPoints: Copper wire answers in the fourth activity
Metal answers in the closing worksheet
successCriteria: I can describe a metal as positive ions in a sea of free electrons
I can explain conduction by the moving electron sea and bending by ion layers sliding
objectives.text: Describe metallic bonding as positive ions in a sea of free electrons
